```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE,
                      warning = TRUE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
```

The code below is the complete executable path for this article. The display
helper reads the table's stored name mapping and changes a copy only.

```{r reader-tools}
library(MIRA)
metric_table <- function(x, columns) {
  mapping <- attr(x, "mira_metric_names")
  actual <- columns
  mapped <- columns %in% names(mapping)
  actual[mapped] <- unname(mapping[columns[mapped]])
  stopifnot(all(actual %in% names(x)))
  answer <- x[, actual, drop = FALSE]
  names(answer) <- columns
  answer
}
```

## A research question before an analysis

This article is an applied capstone for readers who have followed the
[first model](frequentist-long-first-model.html),
[group comparisons](frequentist-long-treatment-groups.html), and
[missing-data principles](frequentist-long-missing-data.html). It supplies its
own data and tools. Expect one coherent dataset, one declared primary
contrast, explicit analysis samples, and a source-only archive; the detailed
[model reference](frequentist-long-advanced-models.html) explains alternative
engines. Understanding regression and interactions is a prerequisite for
using the adjusted conclusion.

Consider a synthetic DME study comparing two hypothetical retinal-treatment
strategies, A and B. The question is whether study-eye BCVA gains over 12 weeks
differ after adjustment for age, lens status and a separate pre-enrolment OCT
screening measurement. BCVA is recorded as ETDRS letter score; higher scores
mean better measured acuity. The primary estimand is the adjusted difference
in mean baseline-to-week-12 gains:
**(Strategy B Week 12 - Strategy B Baseline) - (Strategy A Week 12 -
Strategy A Baseline)**, in ETDRS letters. Positive values favor Strategy B on
this functional scale. We estimate that contrast from the repeated-response
model and inspect the global arm-by-time interaction as a different question.
These generic strategy labels do not represent actual drugs or prescribing
recommendations; the software call alone does not establish causal efficacy.
This is a new 120-person cohort, not a continuation of either complete-data
model demonstration. Its strategy labels apply only to this synthetic DME study.

There are 120 independent adults, each contributing exactly one eligible
study eye. Both eyes are assumed eligible in this synthetic population;
the protocol uses `eye_map` to randomly designate right or left before responses
or allocation are generated. No fellow-eye outcomes enter the analysis. Thus an eye-level ID
also identifies one independent participant. Random assignment is at the
participant/study-eye level. Both-eye or paired-eye treatment designs would
need additional correlation/design handling that this example does not claim.
Four repeated scores from one selected eye remain correlated. This is a
workflow demonstration, not evidence of efficacy or a sample-size justification.

## Generate and inspect the study

The invented working generator has a baseline mean near 56 ETDRS letters,
patient-intercept SD 7 letters and measurement-error SD 3.8 letters. The
expected gain per four-week interval is 1.1 letters for Strategy A and an
additional 1.6 letters for Strategy B. Scores are rounded to letters, and the
complete draw is checked within a plausible interior window without clipping.
No parameter is copied from a treatment trial.

`screening_cmt` is an always-observed, pre-enrolment OCT mean central 1-mm
retinal subfield thickness in micrometres. It precedes the study's BCVA baseline;
it is not the baseline response reused as an adjustment variable. Greater
screening thickness increases missing-follow-up probability in the invented
masking mechanism. Baseline masking is independent. Conditional on this fully
observed predictor, the response-missingness generator is MAR. That is known
from the simulation code, not diagnosed from observed outcomes. OCT thickness
and visual acuity remain different measurements, not interchangeable surrogates.

```{r workflow-data}
set.seed(731921)
n <- 120L
eye_map <- data.frame(
  participant_id = sprintf("DV%03d", seq_len(n)),
  study_eye = sample(c("R", "L"), n, replace = TRUE)
)
eye_map$study_eye_id <- paste(eye_map$participant_id, eye_map$study_eye, sep = "_")
retina_trial <- data.frame(
  study_eye_id = eye_map$study_eye_id,
  treatment_arm = sample(rep(c("Strategy A", "Strategy B"), each = n / 2)),
  age = round(rnorm(n, 66, 9)),
  lens_status = factor(sample(c("Phakic", "Pseudophakic"), n, replace = TRUE)),
  screening_cmt = rnorm(n, 430, 65)
)
subject_intercept <- rnorm(n, 0, 7)
scheduled_weeks <- c(0, 4, 8, 12)
for (j in seq_along(scheduled_weeks)) {
  visit_index <- j - 1L
  retina_trial[[paste0("bcva_t", scheduled_weeks[[j]])]] <- round(
    56 - 0.10 * (retina_trial$age - 66) -
    0.035 * (retina_trial$screening_cmt - 430) +
    1.0 * (retina_trial$lens_status == "Pseudophakic") + subject_intercept +
    visit_index * (1.1 + 1.6 * (retina_trial$treatment_arm == "Strategy B")) +
    rnorm(n, 0, 3.8))
}
visits <- paste0("bcva_t", scheduled_weeks)
retina_complete <- retina_trial
stopifnot(all(as.matrix(retina_complete[visits]) > 10 &
                as.matrix(retina_complete[visits]) < 95),
          all(retina_trial$screening_cmt > 200), all(retina_trial$age > 18))
retina_trial$bcva_t0[sample(seq_len(n), 4)] <- NA_real_
for (j in 2:4) {
  probability <- plogis(-3.2 + 0.40 * (j - 1L) +
                         0.0045 * (retina_trial$screening_cmt - 430))
  retina_trial[[visits[[j]]]][runif(n) < probability] <- NA_real_
}
visit_labels <- c("Baseline", "Week 4", "Week 8", "Week 12")
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(eye_map$participant_id),
  !anyDuplicated(retina_trial$study_eye_id),
  identical(retina_trial$study_eye_id, eye_map$study_eye_id), nrow(retina_trial) == n,
  !anyNA(retina_trial[c("age", "lens_status", "screening_cmt")]))
str(retina_trial)
table(retina_trial$treatment_arm)
colSums(is.na(retina_trial[visits]))
```

The wide table has one study-eye row per participant, linked by `eye_map`.
The MIRA subject identifier is `study_eye_id`; native `patient_factor` fields
carry that identifier. Numeric age and pre-enrolment screening OCT thickness,
plus categorical lens status, are explicitly selected for this working model.
Their coefficients and choice are part of the synthetic design, not an
automatic confounding strategy. The separate `retina_complete` copy makes the
response generation distinct from subsequent missingness masking.

Before computation, audit detection and the final configuration. Explicit
ordering fixes baseline and visit chronology. Labels name occasions but do not
provide elapsed numeric times to models with ordinal-time covariance terms.

```{r workflow-detection}
configuration <- mira_info_long(
  retina_trial, id = "study_eye_id", time_vars = visits,
  time_labels = visit_labels, outcomes = "bcva",
  arm = "treatment_arm", reference_arm = "Strategy A",
  covariates = c("age", "lens_status", "screening_cmt"),
  analyses = c("model", "arm_tests", "plots", "correlations", "outliers"),
  improvement_direction = "higher", stable_threshold = 5,
  alpha = 0.05, p_adjust_method = "holm",
  inspect_only = TRUE, verbose = FALSE
)
configuration$config[c("id", "time_vars", "time_labels", "arm",
                       "reference_arm", "covariates", "analyses")]
configuration$diagnostics
```

## Analyze once and retain the result

The same study now produces descriptive tables, paired changes, group
comparisons, adjusted models, diagnostics and plots. A five-letter stability
band illustrates observed-change classification only: it is not a validated
MCID, a responder definition or a treatment decision threshold. `alpha = 0.05`
requests 95% pointwise intervals. BCVA letter counts are modeled with a Gaussian
working approximation; observed ranges and residual diagnostics remain relevant.

```{r workflow-analysis}
analysis <- mira_info_long(
  retina_trial, id = "study_eye_id", time_vars = visits,
  time_labels = visit_labels, outcomes = "bcva",
  arm = "treatment_arm", reference_arm = "Strategy A",
  covariates = c("age", "lens_status", "screening_cmt"),
  analyses = c("model", "arm_tests", "plots", "correlations", "outliers"),
  improvement_direction = "higher", stable_threshold = 5,
  alpha = 0.05, p_adjust_method = "holm", verbose = FALSE
)
stopifnot(inherits(analysis, "mira_info_long"),
          identical(analysis$time_vars, visits))
class(analysis)
```

Because we explicitly declared `outcomes = "bcva"`, outcome-owned metrics
have that prefix. Each result table's `mira_metric_names` attribute maps
canonical meanings to actual names. The small `metric_table()` display helper
uses this mapping and relabels only its returned copy. It does not modify
the analysis or depend on positional column indices.

## Availability, description, and individual change

Per-visit summaries use observed finite values. Baseline-to-follow-up changes
require both visits, while the Friedman test and complete-profile ICC require
all four visits. These are different analysis populations. A mixed model can
use incomplete outcome histories under its assumptions; it cannot restore
unobserved outcomes or diagnose MNAR dropout from observed values alone.

```{r workflow-description}
knitr::kable(metric_table(analysis$descriptives,
  c("label", "n", "missing", "mean", "sd", "ci_lower", "ci_upper")),
  digits = 2, caption = "Observed study-eye BCVA (ETDRS letters) and pointwise mean intervals.")
analysis$missing$by_time
complete_n <- sum(stats::complete.cases(retina_trial[visits]))
endpoint_n <- sum(stats::complete.cases(retina_trial[c("bcva_t0", "bcva_t12")]))
data.frame(all_participants = nrow(retina_trial), complete_profiles = complete_n,
           baseline_and_week12 = endpoint_n)
```

```{r workflow-change}
baseline_change <- analysis$change[
  analysis$change$from == "bcva_t0", , drop = FALSE]
change_display <- metric_table(baseline_change,
  c("from_label", "to_label", "n", "mean_change", "ci_lower", "ci_upper",
    "cohens_dz", "paired_t_p_adj"))
change_display$paired_t_p_adj <- format.pval(change_display$paired_t_p_adj,
                                           digits = 3, eps = 0.001)
knitr::kable(change_display, digits = 3,
  caption = "Pooled within-participant changes, not treatment effects.")
```

Positive change indicates a measured BCVA letter gain. Pooled change combines
both strategies and cannot establish a between-strategy treatment effect. The paired t interval describes mean
change; paired Wilcoxon tests use a different rank-based question. Pooled
subject trajectories describe heterogeneity and do not provide calibrated
individual treatment-effect estimates.

```{r workflow-figure, fig.cap="Available-case BCVA means (ETDRS letters, higher means better measured acuity) among the synthetic cohort's 120 participants, by assigned arm and scheduled visit. Bars show pointwise 95% Student t intervals for arm means, not intervals for arm differences or paired changes. Availability varies by visit; symbols and line types distinguish groups without color."}
if ("arm_mean_ci" %in% names(analysis$plots)) {
  print(analysis$plots$arm_mean_ci +
          ggplot2::labs(x = "Scheduled visit", y = "Mean study-eye BCVA (ETDRS letters)"))
}
```

## Between-arm quantities and an honest computed conclusion

A visit-specific difference compares observed arm means. A difference in
baseline-to-week-12 changes compares letter gains among endpoint-complete
participants. Neither equals a global interaction test. We show the
unadjusted change contrast first; the adjusted model follows.

```{r workflow-arm-contrast}
arm_change <- analysis$arm_analysis$change_pairwise
endpoint <- metric_table(
  arm_change[arm_change$from == "bcva_t0" &
               arm_change$to == "bcva_t12" &
               arm_change$arm_a == "Strategy A" &
               arm_change$arm_b == "Strategy B", , drop = FALSE],
  c("arm_a", "arm_b", "n_a", "n_b", "difference_in_change_b_minus_a",
    "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "welch_t_p", "welch_t_p_adj")
)
stopifnot(nrow(endpoint) == 1L)
endpoint_display <- endpoint[c("n_a", "n_b", "difference_in_change_b_minus_a",
                               "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "welch_t_p_adj")]
endpoint_display$welch_t_p_adj <- format.pval(endpoint_display$welch_t_p_adj,
                                             digits = 3, eps = 0.001)
knitr::kable(endpoint_display, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = c("n (Strategy A)", "n (Strategy B)", "Difference", "Lower", "Upper", "Holm p"),
  caption = "Week-12 difference in BCVA gains (ETDRS letters): Strategy B minus Strategy A.")
```

In these generated data, the unadjusted week-12 difference in change
(`r endpoint$arm_b` minus `r endpoint$arm_a`) is
`r sprintf("%.2f", endpoint$difference_in_change_b_minus_a)` ETDRS letters
(95% pointwise confidence interval
`r sprintf("%.2f", endpoint$ci_lower)` to
`r sprintf("%.2f", endpoint$ci_upper)`), using
`r endpoint$n_a` and `r endpoint$n_b` endpoint-complete participants.
The within-family Holm-adjusted Welch p-value is
`r format.pval(endpoint$welch_t_p_adj, digits = 3)`.
The sign must be read with the displayed arm order and the higher-is-better
scale. This synthetic association illustrates estimation; a claim of clinical
benefit additionally needs a defensible estimand, missing-data assessment,
study conduct, and externally justified importance threshold.

The confidence interval is pointwise even though the p-value is adjusted.
MIRA adjusts the arm-change pairwise Welch family separately from arm-value
tests, paired time comparisons, and advanced contrasts. It does not automatically
control error over this entire exploratory workflow.

The following audit reconstructs the unadjusted endpoint estimate and its
Welch interval directly from the two sets of paired changes. It verifies
the count, sign, and uncertainty without calling a MIRA helper. This does
not check the adjusted model, whose target follows below.

```{r workflow-unadjusted-audit}
paired <- is.finite(retina_trial$bcva_t0) & is.finite(retina_trial$bcva_t12)
raw_change <- retina_trial$bcva_t12 - retina_trial$bcva_t0
strategy_a_change <- raw_change[paired & retina_trial$treatment_arm == "Strategy A"]
strategy_b_change <- raw_change[paired & retina_trial$treatment_arm == "Strategy B"]
raw_difference <- mean(strategy_b_change) - mean(strategy_a_change)
variance_a <- var(strategy_a_change) / length(strategy_a_change)
variance_b <- var(strategy_b_change) / length(strategy_b_change)
standard_error <- sqrt(variance_a + variance_b)
welch_df <- (variance_a + variance_b)^2 /
  (variance_a^2 / (length(strategy_a_change) - 1) +
   variance_b^2 / (length(strategy_b_change) - 1))
raw_interval <- raw_difference + c(-1, 1) * qt(0.975, welch_df) * standard_error
stopifnot(endpoint$n_a == length(strategy_a_change),
          endpoint$n_b == length(strategy_b_change),
          isTRUE(all.equal(endpoint$difference_in_change_b_minus_a, raw_difference)),
          isTRUE(all.equal(c(endpoint$ci_lower, endpoint$ci_upper), raw_interval)))
```

## Adjusted modeling and model diagnostics

The model contains categorical time, the full time-by-arm interaction,
additive age, lens status, and pre-enrolment OCT thickness, and a random participant intercept.
This is a repeated-response model with baseline as an outcome; it is not an
automatic baseline-adjusted endpoint ANCOVA. A model-based comparison may use
more observations than the complete endpoint contrast above.

```{r workflow-adjustment}
analysis$model[c("covariates_used", "covariates_skipped", "converged",
                 "singular", "warnings", "error")]
if (!is.null(analysis$model$fitted_model)) {
  print(stats::formula(analysis$model$fitted_model))
  model_frame <- stats::model.frame(analysis$model$fitted_model)
  model_ids <- unique(as.character(model_frame$patient_factor))
  endpoint_ids <- retina_trial$study_eye_id[
    is.finite(retina_trial$bcva_t0) & is.finite(retina_trial$bcva_t12)]
  expected_model_ids <- retina_trial$study_eye_id[rowSums(is.finite(
    as.matrix(retina_trial[visits]))) > 0L]
  expected_model_keys <- unlist(lapply(seq_along(visits), function(k) {
    eligible <- is.finite(retina_trial[[visits[[k]]]]) &
      complete.cases(retina_trial[c("treatment_arm", "age", "lens_status", "screening_cmt")])
    paste(retina_trial$study_eye_id[eligible], visit_labels[[k]], sep = "::")
  }), use.names = FALSE)
  model_keys <- paste(as.character(model_frame$patient_factor),
                      as.character(model_frame$time_factor), sep = "::")
  stopifnot(setequal(model_ids, expected_model_ids), !anyDuplicated(model_keys),
            setequal(model_keys, expected_model_keys))
  print(data.frame(observations = stats::nobs(analysis$model$fitted_model),
             subjects = length(model_ids),
             endpoint_complete = length(endpoint_ids),
             model_only = length(setdiff(model_ids, endpoint_ids))))
  print(analysis$model$arm_time_interaction_test)
}
adjusted_conclusion <- "The primary adjusted change contrast was unavailable; inspect module diagnostics."
if (isTRUE(analysis$advanced_tests$emmeans$performed)) {
  interaction <- analysis$advanced_tests$emmeans$arm_time$interaction_tidy
  adjusted_endpoint <- metric_table(
    interaction[
      interaction$arm_factor_pairwise == "Strategy A - Strategy B" &
      interaction$time_factor_pairwise == "Baseline - Week 12", , drop = FALSE],
    c("arm_factor_pairwise", "time_factor_pairwise", "estimate", "lower.CL",
      "upper.CL", "p_raw", "p_primary")
  )
  stopifnot(nrow(adjusted_endpoint) == 1L)
  # Native emmeans grids use external field names, rather than MIRA metrics.
  grid <- analysis$advanced_tests$emmeans$arm_time$tidy
  cell_mean <- function(group, visit) {
    value <- grid$emmean[as.character(grid$arm_factor) == group &
                         as.character(grid$time_factor) == visit]
    stopifnot(length(value) == 1L, is.finite(value))
    value
  }
  expected_change_contrast <-
    (cell_mean("Strategy B", "Week 12") - cell_mean("Strategy B", "Baseline")) -
    (cell_mean("Strategy A", "Week 12") - cell_mean("Strategy A", "Baseline"))
  family <- metric_table(interaction, c("p_raw", "p_primary"))
  stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(adjusted_endpoint$estimate,
                            expected_change_contrast, tolerance = 1e-10)),
            isTRUE(all.equal(family$p_primary,
                             p.adjust(family$p_raw, "holm"))))
  adjusted_conclusion <- sprintf(
    paste0("The primary adjusted difference in baseline-to-week-12 changes ",
           "(Strategy B minus Strategy A) is %.2f ETDRS letters, with pointwise ",
           "95%% interval %.2f to %.2f and Holm-adjusted p-value %s across ",
           "the six arm-by-visit-pair contrasts."),
    adjusted_endpoint$estimate, adjusted_endpoint$lower.CL,
    adjusted_endpoint$upper.CL,
    format.pval(adjusted_endpoint$p_primary, digits = 3)
  )
}
```

`r adjusted_conclusion`

```{r workflow-primary-table}
if (exists("adjusted_endpoint")) {
  primary_display <- adjusted_endpoint
  primary_display$p_raw <- format.pval(primary_display$p_raw, digits = 3, eps = 0.001)
  primary_display$p_primary <- format.pval(primary_display$p_primary, digits = 3, eps = 0.001)
  knitr::kable(primary_display, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
    caption = "Primary adjusted difference in changes: the named contrast retained in the archive.")
}
```

The maximum-likelihood interaction comparison asks whether the model needs
time-varying arm differences. Its p-value is a raw global test. Adjusted simple
arm contrasts at each visit answer a different question. The primary contrast
above instead subtracts two within-arm changes: algebraically,
`(Strategy A - Strategy B) * (Baseline - Week 12)` has the intended
Strategy B-minus-Strategy A change direction. The assertion reconstructs it from
four marginal means. Numeric covariates are held at their reference-grid means
and lens-status levels are averaged equally by emmeans; additive covariates cancel
in this contrast but affect the fitted model and its precision.

The four-cell calculation checks the contrast's orientation and numerical
consistency using the same fitted model and emmeans engine. It is not an
independent validation of the fitted covariance or the engine's interval
calculation. The exact participant-by-visit audit checks the input sample
separately.

The unadjusted and adjusted change contrasts use the same subtraction and
scale. Their samples differ: the former requires both endpoint measurements;
the latter uses available finite responses with complete covariates. Compare
them as estimates under different models and missingness assumptions, rather
than interpreting a changed p-value as proof that adjustment removed bias.

```{r workflow-diagnostics, fig.cap="Conditional residuals (ETDRS letters) from the adjusted primary random-intercept model in the 120-person cohort. The panels assess residual patterns and normal quantiles among used measurements; they do not display confidence or prediction intervals."}
if (!is.null(analysis$model$fitted_model)) {
  local({
    previous <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
    on.exit(par(previous))
    residual <- residuals(analysis$model$fitted_model)
    plot(fitted(analysis$model$fitted_model), residual,
         xlab = "Fitted study-eye BCVA (ETDRS letters)", ylab = "Conditional residual (letters)")
    abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
    qqnorm(residual, main = "Conditional residuals")
    qqline(residual)
  })
}
analysis$diagnostics
```

Residual patterns, singularity, and convergence warnings may invalidate a
simple reading of output. IQR flags in `outliers$by_time` and `outliers$change`
are screening aids, not automatic exclusions. Investigate measurement errors
and prespecify sensitivity analyses rather than deleting inconvenient values.

## Sensitivity with different assumptions

The model request also attempted Gaussian marginal GEE, MMRM, ordinal
random slopes, residual-correlation models, CR2, Kenward-Roger, and rank
longitudinal inference. Their status and hypotheses require individual checks.
The [advanced tutorial](frequentist-long-advanced-models.html) explains each
engine and the result paths in detail.

```{r workflow-sensitivity}
perspectives <- list(
  kenward_roger = analysis$advanced_tests$kenward_roger,
  rank_longitudinal = analysis$advanced_tests$rank_longitudinal,
  mmrm = analysis$advanced_models$mmrm,
  gee_exchangeable = analysis$advanced_models$gee$exchangeable,
  cr2 = analysis$robustness$club_sandwich
)
knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, lapply(names(perspectives), function(name) {
  x <- perspectives[[name]]
  nested_errors <- unlist(x$errors, use.names = TRUE)
  state <- if (!isTRUE(x$performed)) "Unavailable: inspect reason" else
    if (length(c(x$error, nested_errors))) "Partially usable" else
      if (length(x$warnings)) "Completed with warnings" else "Completed"
  data.frame(method = name, performed = isTRUE(x$performed),
    status = state,
    explanation = gsub("[[:space:]]+", " ",
                       paste(c(x$error, x$reason_skipped,
                         if (length(nested_errors)) paste0(names(nested_errors), ": ", nested_errors)),
                         collapse = "; ")),
    warnings = gsub("[[:space:]]+", " ", paste(x$warnings, collapse = "; ")))
})), caption = "Availability does not establish scientific adequacy.")
selected_sensitivity <- analysis$sensitivity[
  analysis$sensitivity$question == "TIME_X_ARM", , drop = FALSE]
sensitivity_display <- metric_table(selected_sensitivity,
  c("question", "method", "n", "p_raw"))
sensitivity_display$p_raw <- format.pval(sensitivity_display$p_raw,
                                         digits = 3, eps = 0.001)
knitr::kable(sensitivity_display, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Interaction perspectives; n follows each method's native sample unit.")
```

The rank method does not use the selected covariates and assumes MCAR for
incomplete profiles. That assumption is deliberately incompatible with this
generator's screening-OCT-dependent response missingness. Its successful computation therefore
does not make it an equally defensible primary analysis. Standard GEE likewise
does not automatically handle general MAR. A suitable likelihood-based mixed
model or MMRM can use available responses under ignorable MAR and the specified
mean/covariance assumptions. None addresses MNAR without additional analysis.

For joint Gaussian coefficient tests, `TIME` and `ARM` include the relevant
interaction terms. A relative-effect rank hypothesis is different. Examine
sample sizes, dropped-term diagnostics, and hypotheses before comparing
sensitivity rows. They are not interchangeable votes.

An inexpensive complete-profile comparison exposes the change in included
participants without another model bundle. It is an additional descriptive
analysis, not an unbiased remedy for response missingness.

```{r workflow-complete-case}
complete_analysis <- mira_info_long(
  retina_trial[stats::complete.cases(retina_trial[visits]), ],
  id = "study_eye_id", time_vars = visits, outcomes = "bcva",
  time_labels = visit_labels,
  arm = "treatment_arm", reference_arm = "Strategy A",
  covariates = character(0), analyses = "arm_tests",
  improvement_direction = "higher", stable_threshold = 5, verbose = FALSE
)
complete_changes <- complete_analysis$arm_analysis$change_pairwise
knitr::kable(metric_table(
  complete_changes[complete_changes$from == "bcva_t0" &
                     complete_changes$to == "bcva_t12" &
                     complete_changes$arm_a == "Strategy A" &
                     complete_changes$arm_b == "Strategy B", , drop = FALSE],
  c("arm_a", "arm_b", "n_a", "n_b", "difference_in_change_b_minus_a",
    "ci_lower", "ci_upper")), digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Complete-profile sensitivity: Strategy B minus Strategy A in baseline-to-week-12 changes.")
```

## Generate and audit a reproducible report bundle

Use a fresh temporary directory so repeated package checks do not replace
research files. `render = FALSE` creates report sources, serialized output,
CSV tables, and a manifest without needing the Quarto executable or LaTeX.
An existing analysis object freezes the analysis used by the report;
`...` analysis arguments are reserved for the direct-data reporting workflow.

```{r workflow-report}
report <- mira_report_freq_long(
  analysis, output_dir = tempfile("mira-dme-bcva-workflow-"),
  output_file = "dme_bcva_study", format = "html",
  title = "Study-eye BCVA gains in a synthetic diabetic macular edema study",
  subtitle = "Observed data, adjusted models, and limitations",
  author = "MIRA tutorial", date = as.Date("2026-10-01"),
  sections = c("methods", "data_quality", "descriptives", "missingness",
               "change", "arms", "models", "diagnostics", "appendix"),
  extra_objects = list(study_eye_map = eye_map,
    unadjusted_endpoint_change = endpoint,
    adjusted_endpoint_change = if (exists("adjusted_endpoint"))
      adjusted_endpoint else adjusted_conclusion),
  max_table_rows = 12, max_table_columns = 9, digits = 3,
  render = FALSE, open = FALSE
)
stopifnot(file.exists(report$source), file.exists(report$payload),
          file.exists(report$runtime), file.exists(report$results_manifest),
          all(file.exists(report$result_files)), !any(report$rendered),
          identical(report$mira_result, analysis))
manifest <- utils::read.csv(report$results_manifest, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
stopifnot(all(file.exists(file.path(report$output_dir, manifest$file))))
utils::head(manifest)
payload <- readRDS(report$payload)
stopifnot(inherits(payload$result, "mira_info_long"),
          identical(payload$extra_objects$study_eye_map, eye_map),
          identical(payload$result$settings, analysis$settings),
          identical(payload$result$descriptives, analysis$descriptives),
          identical(payload$result$change, analysis$change),
          identical(payload$extra_objects$unadjusted_endpoint_change, endpoint))
if (exists("adjusted_endpoint")) {
  stopifnot(identical(payload$extra_objects$adjusted_endpoint_change,
                      adjusted_endpoint),
            identical(payload$result$advanced_tests$emmeans$arm_time$interaction_tidy,
                      analysis$advanced_tests$emmeans$arm_time$interaction_tidy),
            identical(lme4::fixef(payload$result$model$fitted_model),
                      lme4::fixef(analysis$model$fitted_model)),
            identical(as.matrix(vcov(payload$result$model$fitted_model)),
                      as.matrix(vcov(analysis$model$fitted_model))))
}
report$rendered
report$files
```

`files` is empty because no finished document has been rendered. The `.qmd`
source, companion runtime script, and payload must travel together. The CSV
manifest locates exported tables; display truncation does not remove rows from
the underlying analytical object. The checks preserve the input object at
report creation and verify the archived tables, settings, fixed effects, and
covariance after serialization. Native fitted objects contain environments and
external pointers, so whole-object `identical()` after `readRDS()` is not a
meaningful numerical-integrity criterion. Review the report's methods and limitations
before scientific use: report generation does not validate an analysis.

For an actual project, retain the source dataset, prespecified protocol, seed,
saved analysis, report bundle, and software versions in a controlled project
directory. The temporary paths here are for reproducible examples. Use a fresh
directory or deliberately choose `overwrite = TRUE` when regenerating an
existing bundle. The [reporting tutorial](frequentist-long-reporting.html)
covers rendering HTML, PDF, and DOCX with their external requirements.

## Transfer checkpoint: change the endpoint and the subtraction

Before running the solution, adapt the workflow to this request: a colleague
needs the **adjusted baseline-to-week-8 gain in Strategy A minus that in
Strategy B**, with the same covariates and the original six-contrast Holm family.
Identify the native interaction row, predict the direction relative to the
previous Strategy B-minus-Strategy A definition, and find its exported CSV using
the manifest. Do not refit the study or replace the original primary endpoint.

The solution below reuses the fitted grid and the original contrast family.
Changing the endpoint selects another member of that family, so its magnitude
need not equal the primary Week-12 contrast. For the selected Week-8 contrast,
reversing the subtraction negates its estimate and reverses its interval
endpoints while leaving its two-sided p-value unchanged. We preserve explicit labels so the
display does not silently inherit the native contrast's opposite direction.

```{r workflow-transfer}
if (exists("adjusted_endpoint")) {
  target <- interaction[
    interaction$arm_factor_pairwise == "Strategy A - Strategy B" &
      interaction$time_factor_pairwise == "Baseline - Week 8", , drop = FALSE]
  stopifnot(nrow(target) == 1L)
  native_target <- metric_table(target,
    c("estimate", "lower.CL", "upper.CL", "p_primary"))
  transfer <- data.frame(
    endpoint = "Baseline to Week 8",
    subtraction = "Strategy A gain minus Strategy B gain",
    estimate = -native_target$estimate,
    lower = -native_target$upper.CL,
    upper = -native_target$lower.CL,
    p_holm = native_target$p_primary
  )
  expected_transfer <-
    (cell_mean("Strategy A", "Week 8") - cell_mean("Strategy A", "Baseline")) -
    (cell_mean("Strategy B", "Week 8") - cell_mean("Strategy B", "Baseline"))
  stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(transfer$estimate, expected_transfer)))
  csv_record <- manifest[
    manifest$path == "outcome$advanced_tests$emmeans$arm_time$interaction_tidy",
    , drop = FALSE]
  stopifnot(nrow(csv_record) == 1L)
  csv <- read.csv(file.path(report$output_dir, csv_record$file),
                  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  csv_target <- csv[csv$arm_factor_pairwise == "Strategy A - Strategy B" &
                      csv$time_factor_pairwise == "Baseline - Week 8", , drop = FALSE]
  estimate_name <- unname(attr(interaction, "mira_metric_names")[["estimate"]])
  stopifnot(nrow(csv_target) == 1L,
            isTRUE(all.equal(csv_target[[estimate_name]], native_target$estimate)))
  transfer_display <- transfer
  transfer_display$p_holm <- format.pval(transfer_display$p_holm, digits = 3, eps = 0.001)
  knitr::kable(transfer_display, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
    caption = "Transfer solution: a different endpoint and reversed subtraction, with the original Holm family.")
} else {
  cat("Transfer solution unavailable because the adjusted primary module was unavailable; inspect its diagnostics.")
}
```

The exported CSV retains the original numeric estimate and native contrast
labels; it does not contain the relabeled display copy above or the native
table attributes. The metric-name mapping comes from the retained analysis
object. The manifest establishes where this table was exported, while the
four-cell reconstruction establishes the intended subtraction. This
additional contrast is a learning exercise, not a replacement selected after
seeing the original primary result.

## Boundaries and reproducibility record

This workflow estimates observed change, between-arm differences, and adjusted
trajectories from one coherent dataset. The computed endpoint contrast above
is the illustrative scientific conclusion. It is the prespecified adjusted
difference in changes, with the unadjusted contrast as a complementary analysis.
Its model-based interpretation
depends on the stated assumptions. Real studies additionally need validated
measurement scales, a defensible target population, assessment of protocol
deviations, an appropriate multiplicity strategy, and sensitivity to departures
from the missingness model. This tutorial performs no power calculation,
imputation, MNAR analysis, or causal identification exercise.

```{r workflow-session}
packageVersion("MIRA")
sessionInfo()
```


Ophthalmic measurement context: [DRCR visual-acuity protocol](https://public.jaeb.org/drcrnet/stdy/149)
and [DRCR OCT/visual-acuity study in DME](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17123615/).
These support keeping functional BCVA and anatomical thickness distinct. All
effects, schedules, missingness parameters and classification thresholds in
this tutorial are invented. None reproduces a named clinical trial or dictates
clinical care.
